text.en:
During a solar eclipse the sky grew dim at noon and the birds went quiet. Anand watched through special eclipse glasses as the Moon covered the Sun.
"Never look at the Sun directly," his teacher had warned.

A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth and its shadow falls on the Earth. A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon and the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
We never see an eclipse every month because the Moon's orbit is tilted slightly. Solar eclipses must never be watched with the naked eye, as they can harm the eyes. Special filters are needed.
Seasons change because the Earth's axis is tilted and the Earth goes round the Sun once a year. When the northern part tilts towards the Sun it is summer there and winter in the south, and the other way round half a year later.
In a solar eclipse the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth.
In a lunar eclipse the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon.
Never look at the Sun directly, even during an eclipse.
Seasons change because the Earth's axis is tilted as it goes around the Sun.

problem.en: Why do we not see a solar eclipse every month?

text.en: The Moon goes around the Earth every month.

why.en: So it passes between us and the Sun often.

text.en: But its path is tilted a little.

why.en: Its shadow usually misses the Earth.

text.en: So eclipses happen only when the three are lined up.

prompt.en: A friend says seasons occur because the Earth is nearer to the Sun in summer. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Seasons come from the tilt of the Earth's axis, not distance.
When the northern part tilts towards the Sun it gets more direct sunlight.

points.en: Solar eclipse: Moon between Sun and Earth.
Lunar eclipse: Earth between Sun and Moon.
Seasons are due to the tilt of the Earth's axis.
